Elmer Clifton | Elmer Clifton (March 14, 1890 – October 15, 1949) was an American writer, director and actor from the early silent days.  A collaborator of D.W. Griffith, he appeared in "The Birth of a Nation" (1915) and "Intolerance" (1916) before giving up acting in 1917 to concentrate on work behind the camera, with Griffith and Joseph Henabery as his mentors.  His first feature-length solo effort as a director was "The Flame of Youth" with Jack Mulhall.
